title: Exact sequential Fock sampling for rational fermionic Gaussian states

scope.input: An n-mode fermionic Gaussian state supplied by an exact rational Majorana covariance; equivalently, a rational-complex BCS pair matrix with exact covariance construction.
scope.output: One occupation string distributed exactly according to the Born law; pure or mixed states, arbitrary phases, either fixed-parity sector.
scope.quantifiers: For every finite n and every valid rational covariance satisfying the Gaussian-state constraints.

statement: At each mode with covariance entry g=Gamma_(2j-1,2j), outcome s=2x_j-1 has conditional probability (1+s g)/2. For remaining indices a,b the conditional covariance is Gamma^s_ab=Gamma_ab-s(Gamma_ap Gamma_bq-Gamma_aq Gamma_bp)/(1+s g). Iteration samples the exact Fock law.
proof: Occupation projectors are single-mode Gaussian maps. The probability formula is their trace; Wick expansion of the conditioned two-point function gives the rank-two update. Gaussian closure and the Born chain rule prove the output distribution.

cost.arithmetic: O(n^3) rational operations and O(n^2) storage.
cost.bits: Polynomial in n and input height; a conservative prefix/Pfaffian bound is O(n^3 ell) bits for covariance-entry height ell. Exact rational branch probabilities avoid floating-point rare-prefix loss.
cost.randomness: Exact fair-bit Bernoulli draws terminate almost surely with expected polynomial random bits; worst-case coin flips are unbounded. K=ceil(log2(n/epsilon))-bit branch coins give a worst-case finite algorithm with TV error at most epsilon.
cost.energy: Classical sampler consumes no physical energy. Input-state preparation/encoding is separate.

strongest_baseline: Established fermionic linear-optics classical simulation, including Bravyi's Gaussian-map formalism and Terhal–DiVincenzo's noninteracting-fermion circuit simulation.
falsifier_or_boundary: A covariance supplied only as an unqualified noisy floating-point approximation is outside the exact-input theorem; a global interacting filter can make the conditional state non-Gaussian.
unresolved: The rational algorithm is derived but not implemented or proof-assistant checked. It does not solve completion sums for general quota or local filters.

title: Fixed-total-number BCS sampling by Pfaffian coefficient extraction

scope.input: An explicitly supplied rational pure fermionic Gaussian covariance or rational-complex pair matrix and a requested total particle number r.
scope.output: Exact occupation sample from the normalized r-particle sector, or exact detection that the sector has zero norm.
scope.quantifiers: For all finite mode counts n, all valid inputs, and all 0<=r<=n.

statement: For prefix h with k occupied bits, the completion mass in the r-particle sector is the coefficient [z^(r-k)]Q_h(z), where Q_h(z)=Tr[rho (product of prefix projectors)(product of remaining (Pi_0+z Pi_1))]. Wick's rule writes Q_h as one Pfaffian polynomial of degree at most n-|h|. Coefficient ratios give exact next-bit probabilities.
proof: Expand the diagonal generating operator as a sum over completion occupations. The coefficient is exactly the event mass. The Pfaffian minor identity evaluates this generating function from the Gaussian covariance. Child coefficients partition the parent mass, so the chain rule gives the sector-conditioned law.

cost.arithmetic: At most O(n^5) rational field operations by n+1 point evaluations/interpolation per prefix and cubic-time Pfaffians.
cost.bits: All evaluation/interpolation numerators and denominators have polynomial length in n and the pair-matrix encoding length; exact arithmetic has no inverse-sector-probability factor.
cost.energy: No physical postselection attempts are needed by the classical algorithm. A physical rejection implementation would cost 1/p_sector per accepted sample.

strongest_baseline: Grand-canonical Gaussian sampling followed by rejection, expected cost 1/p_sector; direct determinant identities give the unconditioned total-number partition polynomial.
falsifier_or_boundary: This fixes only total particle number. The no-double-occupancy constraint I intersect J=empty is an additional interacting filter and is not represented by this one-parameter coefficient.
unresolved: The interpolation sampler is a checkable derivation from Wick/Pfaffian identities, but has not been implemented or independently reviewed. Priority is not claimed.

title: Parity-sector probabilities contain binary-code coset weight enumerators

scope.input: A product Slater with one fermion in each disjoint two-mode block, followed by measurement conditioned on Hx=s over F_2.
scope.quantifiers: Any finite binary matrix H, syndrome s, and rational site biases p_i; for strictly rational orbital entries the fixed-fugacity subfamily includes z=16/9 via orbital (3/5,4/5).

statement: Pr[Hx=s]=product_i(1-p_i) W_(H,s)(z), where z_i=p_i/(1-p_i) and W_(H,s)(z)=sum_(Hx=s) product_i z_i^(x_i). Exact zero-syndrome evaluation is #P-hard at any fixed rational z>0,z!=1 by the cited weight-enumerator result.
proof: The Slater determinant factors across disjoint orbital pairs, giving the independent Bernoulli law. The probability identity is direct summation over the code coset. Exact-hardness follows by the polynomial-time reduction to binary-code weight enumerators.

cost.input: n disjoint orbital pairs and a binary parity-check matrix; all orbital and filter encoding bits are charged.
cost.exact_count: A polynomial-time evaluator at a fixed nonunit fugacity would evaluate the cited #P-hard code weight enumerator.
cost.positive_cases: For graph-incidence zero syndrome and 0<=z<1, the Ising partition function has an FPRAS; bounded-treewidth Tanner graphs permit exact dynamic programming in 2^O(t) poly(n,L).
cost.energy: The Slater has exactly n fermions; postselection by physical repeated trials costs inverse sector probability.

strongest_baseline: At z=1, probability is exactly 2^(-rank H); graph-incidence zero-syndrome cases reduce to ferromagnetic Ising; bounded-treewidth checks are exactly solvable.
falsifier_or_boundary: At z=1 the claimed generic hardness does not apply; W(1)=2^(dim ker H). The reduction proves exact #P-hardness, not absence of an FPRAS for arbitrary parity constraints.
unresolved: No general relative-approximation hardness is proved for positive weighted code cosets. Nonzero-syndrome Ising FPRAS and arbitrary Tanner graphs remain outside the stated positive cases.

title: CNF-filtered occupation probability is #P-hard on block-product Slater and BCS states

scope.input: A supplied occupation distribution of a product Slater or BCS state and an explicitly listed CNF predicate on designated occupation bits.
scope.quantifiers: For every CNF formula phi on m variables, the constructed instance has probability #SAT(phi)/2^m.

statement: Exact filtered-event evaluation is #P-hard under a one-query metric reduction. An FPRAS for this arbitrary-CNF-filter interface would yield an FPRAS for #SAT and hence NP=RP under the Jerrum–Valiant–Vazirani self-reduction.
proof: Each independent three-mode BCS block (or four-mode rational orthonormal Slater block) has four equiprobable configurations and a fair designated occupation bit. Filtering those m bits by phi yields exactly #SAT(phi)/2^m.

cost.encoding: BCS uses 3m modes with constant integer pair entries; Slater uses 4m modes and 2m particles with entries 0 or plus/minus 1/2; filter size is O(|phi|).
cost.approximation: Relative error is preserved by multiplication by 2^m; exact output has polynomial bit length.
cost.sampling: Unfiltered samples are trivial. Additive TV error must be below 2^-m to distinguish a single satisfying assignment from zero by event frequency.
cost.energy: No physical energy is required for a classical sample; a physical postselection implementation is charged by its accepted-event probability.

strongest_baseline: Independent block sampling exactly solves the unfiltered distribution.
falsifier_or_boundary: This uses an arbitrary CNF predicate. It does not prove hardness for the fixed local no-double-occupancy filter, fixed total number alone, or bare BCS sampling.
unresolved: The result is an interface reduction, not a complexity separation without NP!=RP; nearby constrained-DPP hardness is credited and novelty is not claimed.

title: Chen–Liu complementary log-concave FPRAS covers the N63 quota-filtered Slater count

scope.input: Explicit rational A in Q(i)^(m by r), mode blocks E_j, quotas q_j summing to r, and an acquired feasible quota support.
scope.output: Relative approximation and prefix probabilities for Z=sum_(S quotas) |det A_S|^2; coherent compiler is a separate extension.
scope.quantifiers: The transfer holds when the two homogeneous multiaffine nonnegative log-concave measures have supplied/computable rational value oracles, positive support starts, and polynomial-bit coefficient-range bounds.

statement: Cauchy–Binet gives f(x)=det(A*diag(x)A)=sum_|S|=r |det A_S|^2 x^S. With g(x)=product_j e_(|E_j|-q_j)(x_Ej), [x_all]fg=Z. The Chen–Liu Theorem 5.1 FPRAS therefore applies; prefix conditioning is by derivative/deletion and support is acquired by matroid intersection.
proof: Both factors are homogeneous, multiaffine, nonnegative and log-concave. Clearing denominators gives a polynomial-bit lower bound on positive determinant weights; a Hadamard bound gives a polynomial-bit upper range. Inclusion/exclusion preserves the class, and exact support routines provide zero branches and positive starts.

cost.count: One homogeneous count uses O(m^10 B^2 eta^(-2) log^2(2B/eta)) arithmetic/value-oracle operations, B=m+log(R_f R_g); N63's prefix coherent compiler has a larger O(m^13 B^2 epsilon^(-2) polylog) count component plus support, phase, reversible arithmetic, and gate synthesis.
cost.bits: Chen–Liu Remark A.4 caps exact rational random tapes to obtain a polynomial every-execution bit bound; all oracle outputs and range bounds must have polynomial bit encodings.
cost.energy: This is a classical count/coherent-preparation compiler, not a physical retry sampler; numeric energy cost is not part of this Slater interface.

strongest_baseline: Direct rejection from the original Slater has expected cost det(A*A)/Z and may be exponential. Support-only matroid intersection does not approximate Z.
falsifier_or_boundary: A condition-number-one block Slater can have quota probability 2^-r, refuting a generic polynomial-retry claim. The theorem does not automatically admit generic BCS Pfaffians, no-doublon filters, arbitrary sums or non-log-concave factors.
unresolved: Source theorem and finite-bit cap were audited at decisive sections but not proof-assistant certified; FPRAS, reversible count service, and coherent compiler are unimplemented and unexecuted.

title: All-size parity exchange proves support connectivity but not weighted mixing

scope.input: A nonnegative multiaffine right-half-plane Hurwitz-stable polynomial supported on one parity class.
scope.output: A sharp square-root coefficient-exchange inequality and support connectivity under pair flips.
scope.quantifiers: For every finite variable set and every supported S,T of the same parity, any pivot a in S symmetric-difference T satisfies the N84 inequality.

statement: sqrt(f(S)f(T)) is at most the sum over j in (S triangle T) without a of sqrt(f(S triangle {a,j})f(T triangle {a,j})); constant one is sharp.
proof: Full reciprocal twist by T preserves right-half-plane stability; zeroing outside the symmetric difference gives an even stable polynomial. Setting x_a=1 and x_j=w_j z yields an odd left-half-plane-rooted univariate polynomial. Its positive endpoints obey a0 ad<=a1 a_(d-1); optimize over positive w by Cauchy–Schwarz.

cost.combinatorial: Support graph diameter is at most |S triangle T|/2.
cost.numeric: No coefficient acquisition, bit-costed transition probabilities, or polynomial mixing bound follows from the inequality.
cost.energy: No microscopic transition-energy/Dirichlet cost is supplied.

strongest_baseline: N84 establishes aggregate support connectivity; N85 adds aggregate capacity/relocation under supplied balancing data.
falsifier_or_boundary: For the directed 2q-cycle pair matrix in fixed k=q, only two alternating pair-label supports survive; moves changing fewer than q labels disconnect. The two-mode F_t example has fixed support for all t!=0 but weights |t|^2 and 1.
unresolved: A computable microscopic two-replica energy/conductance bound or a more expressive positive coefficient representation remains missing; route-specific failures do not prove general hardness.

title: Small-loss output sampling for independent two-fermion blocks has quartic error

scope.input: Independent pure two-fermion Gaussian blocks, uniform per-mode vacuum survival eta_i, discarded loss record, followed by supplied Gaussian processing.
scope.output: A positive Gaussian-mixture surrogate sampler for the full final occupation/output law.
scope.quantifiers: For eta_i<1, each block has completion error delta_i<=eta_i^4/(2(1-eta_i)^2); joint TV is at most sum_i delta_i plus separate arithmetic/simulation error.

statement: An explicit finite phase average of pure Gaussian states reproduces the lossy vacuum, one-particle and two-particle sectors while adding only a higher-particle tail of mass delta_i. Tensor products and channel contractivity give the full-law TV bound.
proof: The phase average cancels cross-sector coherences. A scalar product polynomial fixes the vacuum/pair-sector weights; the remaining tail obeys delta_i<=b_i^2/(2a_i), a_i=(1-eta_i)^2, b_i=eta_i^2. Contractivity under later Gaussian processing gives the output bound.

cost.sampling: Polynomial time per sample after covariance acquisition; dense covariance update is O(M^3) arithmetic for M modes, plus finite mixture labels and separately charged precision.
cost.energy: With unit mode energy, expected surviving particles across blocks is 2 sum_i eta_i. No herald record is observed or rejected.
cost.precision: The analytic error is exact; a numeric root/phase implementation still needs a bit-precision bound. The archived float prototype is not certified.

strongest_baseline: Exact Gaussian simulation for eta=0 and the standard unobserved loss channel; the positive completion extends to a quantified small-loss regime.
falsifier_or_boundary: Three-fermion blocks have an eta^3 obstruction; revealing a loss flag changes the local scale to eta^2. The bound is not uniform as eta_i approaches 1 and does not solve filtered-sector sampling.
unresolved: Completion proof is an internal candidate; source-reported diagnostics were not replayed. General mixed/high-particle blocks and certified numerical compilation remain open.

title: Conditional Gaussian-resource lower bound for preparing fermionic codes

scope.input: Independent lossy balanced four-mode magic blocks, Gaussian processing, and a target Majorana-distance codeword.
scope.output: A lower bound on the number of lossy blocks required for constant success/fidelity under the stated architecture.
scope.quantifiers: For a code with k>0, m physical modes, distance d_F>=3, and imported zero-non-Gaussian-gate Gaussian-overlap bound.

statement: At low per-mode survival loss parameter eta, fixed-target concentration costs Theta(eta^-4) blocks. The converse is p(1-epsilon)<= (1+R_eta)^L A^t, where R_eta=eta^4/[4(1-eta)^2], A=1-H_2^{-1}(k/m), and t=floor((d_F-1)/2).
proof: The balanced four-mode block has exact Gaussian robustness R_eta in the stated low-loss branch; multiplicative tensor domination and branchwise Gaussian-preserving monotonicity combine with Tang et al.'s Theorem 2 zero-gate overlap cap. Independent filters attain the exponent for fixed target 0<q<1.

cost.blocks: For fixed target and constant p, L=Omega(d_F/eta^4); the separable filter upper is O(eta^-4) for one fixed target block.
cost.energy: Each source block has expected surviving particle number 4 eta; physical ancillas and measurements for filtering are charged separately.
cost.precision: Filter s=eta(1-q)/(q(1-eta)); relative filter error xi gives explicit target shift and success-ratio change in leaf-08.

strongest_baseline: Independent Gaussian filters attain the fixed-target eta^-4 exponent; this is a resource-conversion bound, not a sampling-hardness claim.
falsifier_or_boundary: Imported code-overlap theorem is used only at zero extra non-Gaussian gates. No complexity separation, code-preparation achievability, arbitrary hardware, or q=1 claim follows.
unresolved: Tang's source theorem is not independently certified here; global experimental or fault-tolerant attainability and broader prior art remain open.
